1874964994674295128 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 187 🔁 26
I keep being asked to give an overview of memetics. I'll take a stab at it in thread form. 🧵👇 https://t.co/njQicovY7P
  [Quoting @Cantide1: @Morphenius My buddy doesn't understand memetics, can you give a short primer on memes and memetics?]

===

1874965309268144581 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 44
Quite a lot of shamanism and magic amounts to attempts at memetic engineering. Exorcizing spirits, putting up wards, etc.

And some of it works! Much like ancient Romans could build aqueducts centuries before Newton invented the modern version of physics.
↓
1874965321377095939 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 35
For instance, my view of attachment theory came from an explicitly shamanic attempt to heal my Torn style. And it helped a lot! The ritual made it possible for me to start dating again. https://t.co/sWROelt4L0
  [Quoting @Morphenius: The true (IMO) names for the four attachment styles are:  • Good • Clingy • Cold • Torn  (I tongue-in-cheek want to name the last one "F*cked" but I think "Torn" is way clearer.)]
↓
1874965333427314825 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 33
But thoughts are memetic. Ideas about mechanical engineering aren't subject to physics the way the idea of spirits is subject to memes.

So without a precise science, shamanism risks becoming a vector for memetic parasites.

("You'll lose your soul if you dabble with magic.")
↓
1874965345372680493 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 37
So you end up with some "self-hiding" spirits, and some spirits that insist we're not allowed to consider a spirit world at all.

Wokism started insisting on not being named for instance. And scientific culture tends to insist that memes are "just a metaphor".
↓
1874965357259366679 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 26 🔁 2
(Never mind that, say, an elephant is "just a metaphor" too. Unless scientific culture would like to argue that there's some ephemeral "essence of elephant" that's objectively real and yet independent of the physics & biochemistry constituting an elephant…?)
↓
1874965369179488366 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 24
The name for memetics really should be "the study of spirits" in Greek. Like astronomy should be "the study of stars" if astrology hadn't gotten the name first. Likewise, memetics cannot really reclaim its rightful name from psychology.
↓
1874965380953002206 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 31
That said, IMO Carl Jung was in fact trying to bridge shamanism & science. And I think memetics offers clarification & precision to a lot of his ideas.
↓
1874965392864817455 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 39 🔁 1
For instance, archetypes are basically gravitational attractors in memetic evolution. When a meme is trying to find a viable form, some long-proven patterns (like "Mother" or "Warrior") can act as possible building blocks. Many of those patterns are thus "immortal" memes.
↓
1874965404810109043 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 24
This starts to spell out what a "god" might be, for real. Some "unbidden" thoughts will arise archetypically. Thus, much like "Free Palestine" shows up through many people, so can (say) the Warrior — a FAR more ancient force than this young memetic upstart.
↓
1874965416692580739 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 23
That said, IMO Jungian psychology tends to get lost in myth the same way shamanism & magic do. I don't mean to idolize it. I'm pointing out that the field of memetics has been trying to arise for a long time & has a LOT of overlap with both psychology & spirituality.
↓
1874965428336005495 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 31 🔁 1 [(SEED) type=semantic_search]
Eg, many memes operate through your implicit sense of self. Some memes are quite miserable to host, but "you" can't get rid of them b/c they're part of "you". So what do?

That's a basic conundrum many religions orient to. Christian salvation, for instance, or Buddhist no-self.
↓
1874965440172368348 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 35 🔁 3
I have hope that a mature science of memetics can do justice to spirituality & religion. The scientific memeplex had its teenage rebellion against the Church. Teens do that to individuate. But now maybe science can care for what the Church was calling "the human soul".
↓
1874965452272828677 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 28
There's a lot more to say. Memetics is as huge as biology. The big diff for an overview is that folk already know what plants & animals are. I'm having to point at psychofauna AT ALL, w/o a clear taxonomy, while keeping it near science instead of it all becoming just mystical.
↓
1874965464109240471 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 33
So I hope this has served well as a solid, if partial, intro.

Feel free to ask me whatever about memes. I'm not The Authority™ on the topic, but I've thought about & studied memes explicitly for a good while. I'm happy to share my impressions.

/fin
↓
1874965475723301147 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 14
Here are some further resources for the curious:
↓
1874965487505068381 [2025-01-02] @Morphenius 💜 16

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand traces a multi-year evolution of the concept of 'self as coordination mechanism' across philosophical, therapeutic, and spiritual frameworks. The boundary object is Andres Gomez Emilsson's 2024 tweet framing self as 'a religion that your parts follow,' which crystallizes earlier explorations of parts-work (IFS), no-self experiences, and memetics. The discourse is primarily constructive rather than dialectical—participants build on each other's models (cells-to-organism analogies, prediction as fundamental category, memetic parasites) rather than arguing. High cohesion around a core metaphor-cluster, with practical utility for meditation practitioners and community organizers thinking about coordination at multiple scales.

title: “You” Is a Religion Your Brain Runs
summary:
Andres Gomez Emilsson (@algekalipso) drops the banger that detonates the whole strand: **“You” are a religion that your parts follow in order to coordinate with each other.** The spicy extension is that a “no-self” experience is basically *deconversion*—your internal subagents stop treating one central narrative as sacred, then maybe “convert” to a meta-framework that lets them reorganize more flexibly.

Once that metaphor lands (July 2024), @DefenderOfBasic immediately pokes the one question that makes it real instead of just poetic: **if the religion of “you” dies, why don’t enlightened/no-self people become total inconsistent chaos?** Andres answers: they often *do* report less internal coherence, but they’re calmer about contradiction because no subagent gets to be The Pope of the psyche. That’s when the thread peaks into vivid governance metaphors: @DefenderOfBasic calls it “a little democracy,” @slimepriestess says for them it’s “more like a polycule” where consent/compassion/boundaries keep the system coordinated, and @christophcsmith reframes identity as “mutual obligation” between past/future selves rather than a single continuous ruler.

The afterglow is everyone trying to generalize the coordination idea across scales: earlier seeds compare God/civilization to a super-organism self (via @nosilverv paraphrasing Joscha Bach), Malcolm Ocean (@Malcolm_Ocean) does the “my cells’ relationship with me ≈ my relationship with God” analogy, and later @DefenderOfBasic + @howwardroark riff that self-awareness might have emerged from solving coordination among conscious subagents—mirroring how religion historically coordinated humans out of lose-lose conflict. By 2025, Morphenius (@Morphenius) plugs memetics into the same socket: **memes operate through your implicit sense of self**, and religions (Christian salvation, Buddhist no-self) are partly about unhooking from “miserable” memes you can’t drop because they feel like *you*. Why care: it’s a clean mental model that ties therapy parts-work, meditation/no-self, religion, and even memetics into one practical question—*what’s coordinating your inner coalition, and can you upgrade the constitution without your whole system falling apart?*
